issue: #594 — the §8.11 forced-order material carriage lane. Rows first pinned here, in answer to the round-N review finding that §8.11 published a cost claim with no exec-ledger measurement behind it while §8.10's precedent and the #519/#523 gate-that-cannot-fail doctrine require one.
spec: docs/spec/midgard-tx.md §8.11 (the mint is the only on-chain reader of an order's material; carriage is prover-chosen per non-empty field and the door entry point MUST be the whole-materialising one), with §5.1/§5.3 for the preimage grammar and strides, §5.4 for the byte bounds, §8.3/§8.4 for `K` and the tier-3 partition, and §8.6 for the certificate manifest
note:
§8.11 publishes a cost for the tx-order mint and nothing measured it. These rows are that measurement, taken through `run-focused-check.mjs` against `lib/midgard/user-events/tx-order-v1.test.ak`, and they split the published claim in two because `whole_view` does.

**What the claim says.** §8.11 requires the *whole-materialising* door entry point (`authenticated_whole_field_view`) rather than the lazy one, because this mint touches no items and a tier-3 order authenticated lazily would have its manifest checked and its named chunk reference inputs never read. It then prices that choice: \"Its cost is §12.5's tier-2 per-step full-preimage re-hash, bounded by §5.4's 32,768-byte aggregate over all nine fields.\"

**Where it holds.** `whole_view` settles §5.1 count consistency by arithmetic for the five fixed-stride fields (0, 1, 3, 4, 7), so for those the only cost that grows with the field is the one `blake2b_256` over its preimage — which is exactly what the claim says. `tx_order_mint_material_at_the_aggregate_bound` measures the nine-field walk at §5.4's bound with every spare byte in field 0: nine door openings (three of them witness-set fields, which re-derive the §2.5 pairing per opening), 32,742 bytes hashed, and the widened field carried through tier 3 at §8.3's maximum chunk count of three. It measures 2,284,621 mem / 906,978,408 cpu whole-test, against a fixture-only control of 759,097 / 391,345,191 — so the mint's own share is about 1.53M mem, 12% of the §3.3 memory basis, with the byte term costing roughly 2.4 mem per byte carried.

**Where it does not.** For the four variable-width fields (2 outputs, 5 mint, 6 script witnesses, 8 redeemers) `whole_view` cannot check §5.1's count by arithmetic and runs `walk_to_end`, one `field_read_range` and one item head per item. That per-item term is not in §8.11's sentence and it dominates everything else. The two variable-width rows read the same nine-field shape with the spare width in field 8 at 250 and at 500 minimum-width items, and their difference prices the walk at **21,062.03 mem and 6,275,214 cpu per item** (5,265,508 mem / 1,568,803,513 cpu over 250 items). Extrapolating the pair gives an intercept of 1,892,421 mem, so the §3.3 memory basis is reached at about **536 items** — the memory axis binds; cpu at that cardinality is around 4.02G against the 8G basis. Both rows are deliberately kept as the pin rather than a comfortable pair well below it: the upper row sits at 94% of the memory basis, so a walk that gets dearer per item crosses the basis in this ledger rather than in a later wave.

**The over-basis reading, and why it is not a row here.** The worst shape this mint admits at §5.4's bound is nine non-empty fields with the spare width in a variable-width slot at minimum item width: `3 + 2·16,254 = 32,511` bytes in field 8 plus the other eight slots at their minimum non-empty width is an aggregate of exactly 32,768, carried tier 3 at three chunks. It measures **344,075,442 mem / 102,708,068,556 cpu** — 26.1x the §3.3 memory basis, 12.8x its cpu basis, and 20.9x / 10.3x the raw mainnet `maxTxExUnits` before any reserve. The reading is 0.04% off the linear extrapolation from the two rows below, so the pair genuinely prices it. It is not a row because a within-basis ledger records only `within` rows (see `exec-ledger-within-basis-v1.mjs`), and the q1x-style `basisFit:\"exceeds\"` vocabulary requires an `errata` cross-reference into a normative erratum that §8.11 does not yet carry. Publishing an over-basis row against a non-existent erratum would be the recorded-infeasibility check answered with a promise, so the reading, its one-line reproduction and the residual are recorded on #594 for #580's re-measurement pass instead.

**What these rows do NOT claim.** (1) That the shapes measured are valid L2 transactions. They are the worst shapes *this mint* admits, which is what bounds its cost: the mint authenticates a field's preimage against the creator's own committed hash and never decodes an item's content, so a variable-width field of one-byte items passes the door whatever the field's own §5.3/§5.5/§5.6 grammar says about it, and it is the creator who commits to the bytes. (2) That §5.4's aggregate is enforced here. `whole_view` enforces the **per-field** bound (`total_length <= max_transaction_aggregate_field_bytes`) and nothing in `verify_order_material` sums the nine, so nine fields at 32,768 each — 294,912 bytes — are equally admissible to the mint; the aggregate is a consensus-side property of a valid L2 transaction, not a mint guard, and §8.11's wording reads it as a bound on the mint. (3) A machine-checked decomposition. The within-basis shape judges absolute rows and publishes no `derived` subtraction, so the aggregate-bound row and its control bracket the mint's own cost rather than isolating it; a reader who needs the door cost isolated per tier has that in `native-tx-carriage-exec-ledger-v1.json` (§8.10). Rows are whole-test readings and therefore include fixture construction, the same convention the Q21/Q31 ledgers use, which is why a row moves when a fixture is simplified.

Regenerate with `MIDGARD_AIKEN_BIN=<fork> node scripts/verify-tx-order-mint-exec-ledger-v1.mjs --update`, and move any reported number in the same commit. `--update` rewrites the raw mem/cpu rows; it does NOT rewrite `basisFit`, and it is not a bypass — a row or selector that did not run, or a fresh reading that contradicts a `within` judgement, fails in update mode too and the ledger is not rewritten. Provisional on the same footing as every other ledger in this directory: formal closure is Phase 7's, against the Phase-6 blueprint.

**#606 re-take, 2026-08-16 — the E2 certificate repair, and the fitted ceiling falls to 536.** Bisected against pristine `git archive` builds of the intervening commits rather than assumed: the pexcludes rider `139a8ca3` leaves every row below identical to the batch base `854fea09` to the unit, so the whole of the movement is the E2 repair commit `d528e00b` — constant certificate asset name, mint-welded `field_hash`, the door's new equality of that `field_hash` against the commitment derived from the anchored structures, and the deletion of `carriage_reaches_the_anchor`.

**The aggregate-bound pair.** The row rose by **28,233 mem / 39,633,351 cpu** and its fixture-only control by **16,610 / 37,442,377**, so the mint's own share rose by 11,623 mem / 2,190,974 cpu — from about 1.51M to about 1.53M mem, 11% of the §3.3 basis to 12%. This is the one shape in the ledger that carries a field through tier 3 at §8.3's maximum chunk count, so it is the one that pays for the certificate the repair changed, and most of the cpu arrived in the *fixture*: what a test must build to present a certificate moved further than what the mint charges to check one. No decomposition across the repair's four changes is published, for the reason `native-tx-carriage-exec-ledger-v1.json` states at its own certificate rows — nothing measured here separates them.

**The two variable-width rows moved by a constant** — **+6,500 mem / +1,040,000 cpu each**, identical at 250 and at 500 minimum-width items. Being identical on both rows of the pair, it cancels out of the difference: the per-item price is **unchanged to the unit** at 21,062.03 mem and 6,275,214 cpu, and only the intercept rose, 1,885,921 → 1,892,421 mem. **That is enough to move the published ceiling down one item, 537 → 536**, and it is re-derived above rather than left standing. It remains what it always was in this lane — an **extrapolation from the two rows**, not a bisected reading: unlike §12.7 and §12.8, this lane has no boundary-pair selectors pinning its crossing, and adding them is not this re-take's work. The upper row still sits at 94% of the memory basis, so the pair still prices the crossing from close beside it.

**One figure here is deliberately NOT re-taken, and this is the record of that.** The over-basis reading above — 344,075,442 mem / 102,708,068,556 cpu for the 16,254-item shape — was measured once, before #606, and recorded on #594; no selector in `lib/midgard/user-events/tx-order-v1.test.ak` pins it, so re-taking it would mean adding one, which is outside this re-take. Extrapolating the *re-measured* pair puts that shape at about 344,234,689 mem, 0.05% from the pre-#606 reading, so the 26.1x / 12.8x judgements it carries are unaffected — but the reading itself is pre-#606 and is flagged as such rather than silently re-pinned to arithmetic. No `basisFit` moved; every row here was and remains `within`.

basis.source: GOAL_SPEC §3.3 — 20% margin off the supported L1 floor MIDGARD_CONSENSUS_LIMITS_V1.minSupportedL1MaxTxMemoryUnits of 16,500,000 mem. Provenance, exactly as §3.3 states it: the captured in-repo artifact is the mainnet parameter snapshot in docs/midgard/decisions/0001-cardano-l1-transaction-capability-floor.md, Conway epoch 645, observed 2026-07-24.

modules.neutralisationNote: Both selectors are mutation-verified rather than assumed. (1) `tx_order_mint_material_fixture_sits_at_the_aggregate_bound` is the shape guard, and it is the reason a re-take cannot quietly re-pin a cheaper row: it asserts nine non-empty commitments, an aggregate of 32,742 that one more field-0 item at §5.3's 40-byte stride would push past §5.4's bound, the widened field at 32,523 bytes above §8.3's `K` with `expected_chunk_count` equal to `max_tier3_chunk_count`, field 0's stride and field 8's `walk_derived_stride` marker, both variable-width read cardinalities, and — at a width where the quadratic fold is affordable to run beside it — that the fixtures' doubling builder emits exactly what `encode_field_preimage` would. Shrink any fixture and this selector goes red before the row is re-pinned. (2) `tx_order_mint_material_at_the_aggregate_bound_refuses_a_tampered_tail_chunk` is the discrimination guard: neutralising `whole_view`'s `expect field_commitment(preimage) == expected_hash` in `lib/midgard/native-tx-field-access-v1.ak` turns it red, and the check report names that exact line as the failure it traps. The vector is honest about isolating that one guard — the certificate is the one a real certification produced, its digest vector is over the real chunks, every named chunk is the right length, and field 0 is fixed-stride so §5.1's count arithmetic is still satisfied by the tampered bytes. It is also what makes §8.11's *whole-materialising* requirement falsifiable: under the lazy tier-3 form this mint touches no item, so nothing would read the substituted chunk and the vector would pass. The door's other guards are covered by this module's small-shape negatives (positional order, exhaustion in both directions, the §8.4 lower bound, the missing policy token, the §2.4 declared-length disagreement) rather than restated at the bound, because a 32,742-byte fixture isolates none of them better than a 41-byte one does.
